text:
anna: FYI shelf-9 (usw1) popped a NVMe burst + router egress tail at 02:12 UTC. Several dedicated slices saw transient 99p spikes ~1.8s. Customers hit timeouts.
devin: I see the same. tx_burst and kvcache regen on host-09-3. suspect a dataset ingestion job. can we try a tiny fallback to spare the shelf while we ID tenant?
priya: recommend 10% fallback to warm-reserve + immediate per-tenant shaping for top writers. if fallback helps we can avoid heavy migrations. cost note: warm-reserve delta ~+$300/hr.
mike: quick commands:
```
# 10% fallback
curl -X POST "http://router-api/v1/routing/fallback" -d '{"from":"slice-ded-12","to":"warm-reserve-usw1","fraction":0.10}'
# shape tenant-109 to 60Mbps
curl -X POST "http://router-api/v1/tenants/109/shape" -d '{"bandwidth_mbps":60}'
```
priya: also set spillback_window=45s to avoid oscillation while we test.
infra-bot: [ACTION] 02:14 UTC fallback 10% applied to slice-ded-12 by mike. Telemetry tag=burst-circuit-5544332211. Observed 99p down to ~220ms after 75s. alert-id: A-5544332211.
anna: good delta. can we run a quick top-writer query and paste results? will decide move vs shaping.
infra-bot: top_writers (01:58-02:12): ["tenant-109","tenant-707","tenant-402"], avg_write_iops [5800,2100,900].
devin: target tenant-109 shaping applied. if tail remains >400ms after 8m we do ephemeral carveout: create fractional slice, live-migrate tenant-109, replay traffic for 30m.
priya: please note quarantine rule proposal: auto-fractionalize if a tenant causes >2 NVMe spikes in 6h. file created: INFR-9001.
mike: proceeding to 30% fallback now per priya. will monitor for warm-reserve latency >700ms (rollback threshold).
infra-bot: 02:18 UTC fallback increased to 30%. 99p now ~160ms. warm-reserve 99p = 210ms. continuing to monitor.
anna: thanks all. logging everything in INFR-9001 and will draft a short post-incident note after stabilization. reactions: :thumbsup:
